pipeline.title: Reasoning pipeline

tips.title: Breaks one analysis into 7 visible reasoning steps — each one you can see and challenge, instead of being handed a conclusion.
tips.materials: Lists the facts used, each tagged by reliability (strong/medium/weak/unverifiable); it never fakes what it couldn't verify.
tips.anomaly: Picks the most 'off', highest-explanatory anomaly as the entry point — anomalies are the cracks in a structure.
tips.skeleton: Strips emotion and stance, reducing the event to five neutral elements: subject / object / mechanism / harmed / benefited.
tips.mechanism: Digs the causal chain surface -> deeper -> bottom, down to a transferable underlying structure, and maps the flow of interests.
tips.game: Works out where the players' game settles, and tests the structure against isomorphic cases from other domains.
tips.scenario: Lists key variables and possible branches, each with a probability and observable early-warning signals.
tips.judgment: Gives core judgments with confidence, each carrying a 'falsifiable condition' — what would prove it wrong.
tips.adversarial: Attacks its own conclusion from the strongest opposing view (devil's advocate) and audits its own cognitive biases.

pipeline.disagreeHint: Write an objection or a follow-up question: a rebuttal gets full reasoning for why it's absorbed or held; a question (like "why?") gets a direct answer one layer deeper, not just a verdict on your view.
pipeline.disagreePlaceholder: Rebut: the anomaly entry is wrong; the real key is… / or ask: why does this happen? What's the deeper cause?
